chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about sharing food with the Jew and the Christian, so he said, 'There is no harm if it is from your food.' And I asked him about sharing food with the Magian, so he said, 'If he performs ablution, there is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sharing food with Jews, Christians, and Magians in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the conditions for sharing meals with non-Muslims, distinguishing between the People of the Book and Magians. For Jews and Christians, permissibility is linked to the food source being from one's own provisions, while for Magians, the condition is their performance of ablution (*wudu*), reflecting the juristic view that their ritual purity status allows for such social interaction.
